about: What each engine is started with. Prime95 gets one worker with one core per test (NumWorkers, CoresPerTest, NumCores), and must not bind its threads itself (EnableSetAffinity=0), or it spreads over cores, or never gets going inside the one processor it is confined to, and a single-core test means nothing: with the settings of 1.x it reported no finished FFT size in seven minutes, with these it does within seconds. y-cruncher is started with a settings file that names the logical processors it runs on (its stress verb cannot): from the command line it starts a thread for every logical processor of the machine, which take turns on the one it is confined to; its logfile switch has to precede the verb.
